What We Do

Full-Service Sleep Medicine Revenue Cycle Management

Sleep medicine billing requires precise polysomnography type coding, split-night study identification, home sleep test vs. in-lab study distinction, and CPAP supply and follow-up coordination. PMEX manages every element from the sleep study report to payment posted.

Polysomnography Coding

95810 (diagnostic PSG) and 95811 (titration PSG) coded from the study type performed.

Split-Night Study Billing

Split-night PSG (95811 with modifier 52) billed correctly when diagnostic and titration in one night.

Home Sleep Testing

HST codes (95800 to 95806) billed by the type of monitoring and channels recorded.

CPAP Initiation and Management

CPAP management E/M coded with correct follow-up codes and compliance data review.

Oral Appliance Authorization

OAT prior authorization managed with sleep study and CPAP failure documentation.

Multiple Sleep Latency Testing

MSLT (95805) coded separately from the overnight PSG on the same admission.

Common Sleep Medicine Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Full-night PSG billed when a split-night study was performed, applying the wrong code.

PMEX reads the sleep study report to confirm study type and codes split-night with 95811 plus modifier 52 when applicable.

CPAP follow-up visit not billed when the provider reviews compliance download data.

PMEX identifies CPAP compliance review visits from the clinical documentation and codes them at the correct E/M level.

Oral appliance prior authorization submitted without CPAP failure documentation.

PMEX compiles CPAP intolerance or failure documentation before submitting OAT authorization requests.

Home sleep test channels not confirmed before code selection, causing underpayment.

PMEX confirms the number of channels recorded from the HST report and applies the correct 95800-series code.

MSLT not billed separately when performed the day after an overnight PSG.

PMEX submits 95805 (MSLT) separately from the preceding overnight PSG when both are documented.

Sleep study denied because physician order was not on file before the study was performed.

PMEX confirms the ordering physician order is on file before the sleep study is scheduled and billed.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Sleep Medicine Billing

Sleep medicine practices lose 14 to 24 percent of revenue to study type miscoding, CPAP follow-up omissions, and oral appliance authorization gaps.

PATTERN 01

Split-Night Study Billed as Full-Night Titration

Patient undergoes diagnostic portion and CPAP titration in a single night. 95811 (titration PSG) submitted without modifier 52. Payer adjudicates at the full titration rate but the study was split-night. On audit, the study documentation does not match the code. Recoupment risk created.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the sleep study report to confirm split-night vs. full-night study type and applies 95811 with modifier 52 for split-night studies, matching the code to the documented study structure.

PATTERN 02

Oral Appliance Auth Denied, CPAP Failure Not Documented

Patient requests oral appliance therapy for OSA. Prior authorization submitted. Denied: no documentation that CPAP was tried and failed or is contraindicated. Device cost: $800 to $2,000. No retroactive auth available.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX compiles the CPAP trial documentation (duration of trial, compliance data, reported intolerance) before submitting the oral appliance authorization request, and manages contraindication documentation when applicable.

PATTERN 03

MSLT Not Billed After Overnight PSG

Overnight PSG followed by daytime MSLT for narcolepsy evaluation. 95810 (PSG) billed. 95805 (MSLT, $420) not submitted. Billing team assumes the MSLT is bundled with the PSG. It is a separately payable service on the following calendar day.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies MSLT studies from the sleep lab schedule and submits 95805 separately from the overnight PSG. The MSLT is billed on the calendar day it was performed, confirmed from the study report.

Questions

Sleep Medicine Billing Questions Answered

95810 is a diagnostic polysomnography without CPAP titration. 95811 is a polysomnography with CPAP titration. Split-night studies use 95811 with modifier 52 to indicate the study was not a full-night titration.

HST codes (95800 to 95806) are selected based on the type of monitoring and the number of physiological channels recorded. We confirm the channels from the HST report before selecting the code.

Yes. Physician visits to review CPAP compliance data and adjust therapy are billed as E/M visits at the appropriate level. We identify compliance review visits from the clinical documentation and code them correctly.

Most payers require a sleep study documenting OSA (AHI of 5 or greater) and documentation that CPAP was tried and failed or is contraindicated. We compile this documentation before submitting the authorization request.

Yes. The MSLT (95805) is separately billable when performed on the calendar day following the overnight PSG. It is not bundled with the PSG.

Within 30 days, with sleep study coding workflows and CPAP follow-up billing active from day one.
